blocks.text: To define a structured method for shifting the Company's operations towards cleaner energy and lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by increasing renewable power, upgrading to energy-efficient technology, recovering waste energy, controlling fluorinated gas emissions, reducing IT energy use and building employee capability for a low-carbon workplace.
This SOP applies to all departments, employees and contract workers of Navitas Solar Pvt Ltd, and covers:

Purchased grid electricity, electricity from the 1,701.00 kWp rooftop solar PV plant and any renewable electricity procured from external sources
Production equipment and utilities, including stringers, laminators, framing lines, testers, compressors, pumps, motors, HVAC and lighting
Equipment that produces recoverable heat, such as air compressors, laminators, chillers and DG sets (where installed)
Equipment containing fluorinated gases, such as air conditioners, chillers, refrigerators, vehicle air conditioning, SF6-insulated switchgear and clean-agent fire suppression systems
IT infrastructure, including the server room / network racks, UPS systems, computers, printers and other office electronics
Procurement of new or replacement energy-using equipment and new energy projects
Training and awareness of all employees on energy and climate topics
The Company aims to:

Raise the share of renewable electricity in total energy consumption year on year.
Reduce specific energy consumption (kWh per MW of modules produced) through technology and equipment upgrades.
Recover usable heat from processes and utilities wherever technically and economically viable.
Prevent leakage of refrigerants and other fluorinated gases, and move to low-GWP alternatives.
Reduce the energy consumed by IT infrastructure and office electronics.
Build employee knowledge and ownership of energy saving and low-carbon practices.
Measure, report and continually reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions.

body.text: 6.2.3 Evaluation and Approval

Collect 12 months of load profile and electricity bills.
Carry out a technical feasibility check (available area, structural stability, grid connectivity, shading).
Prepare a techno-commercial comparison: cost per unit vs. grid tariff, payback, expected annual generation and tCO2e reduction.
Confirm regulatory requirements (connectivity, metering arrangement, Electrical Inspector approval, open access approval as applicable).
Submit the proposal to the Plant Head / Top Management for approval.
On approval, execute the project or contract through the Purchase department and commission it with documented test results.
6.2.4 Metering and Renewable Energy Accounting

Every on-site RE system shall have a dedicated generation meter; purchased RE shall be supported by invoices, energy accounts or certificates.
Meter readings shall be recorded monthly in the Renewable Energy Register.
RE share (%) = Renewable electricity consumed (kWh) ÷ Total electricity consumed (kWh) × 100
Renewable attributes that are sold or transferred to another party (e.g. RECs sold) shall not be counted as the Company's renewable consumption.

Retain the commissioning protocol, test reports, as-built drawings and warranty documents of the 1,701.00 kWp plant.

Ensure safe access to the roof (fall protection, permit-to-work) for all cleaning and maintenance activities.

Each proposal shall be documented with: baseline consumption, expected annual saving (kWh and ₹), investment, simple payback, expected tCO2e reduction, impact on production and safety, and implementation timeline. 6.3.4 Measurement and Verification of Savings

Measure consumption of the equipment or area for a representative period before the change.
Implement the upgrade and allow it to stabilise.
Measure consumption for an equivalent period under comparable production conditions.
Calculate savings: Energy saved (kWh) = (Baseline SEC − New SEC) × Production in the period.
Record the result in the Energy Efficiency Project Register and update the baseline.

For CHP units: Overall efficiency (%) = (Electrical output + Useful thermal output) ÷ Fuel energy input × 100.

body.text: 6.5.2 Leak-Tightness Checks and Repairs

Carry out leak checks at a frequency based on gas charge and criticality (minimum frequency: [To be confirmed by the Company]).
Use trained and competent technicians (in-house or service provider) and electronic leak detectors.
Locate and repair leaks before recharging; repeated top-ups on the same unit require root-cause analysis.
Never vent refrigerants or SF6 to the atmosphere; monitor SF6 gas density / pressure gauges on switchgear.
Record every top-up quantity in the F-Gas Register.
6.5.3 Shift to Lower-Impact Refrigerants

New or replacement cooling equipment shall preferably use lower-GWP refrigerants (for example R-32, R-290 or HFO-based blends), subject to safety and technical suitability.
Avoid purchasing new equipment using HCFC R-22 or high-GWP HFCs (such as R-404A) where suitable alternatives exist, in line with India's commitments under the Montreal Protocol and its Kigali Amendment.
Plan phased replacement of old, leak-prone or high-GWP equipment as part of the capital plan, starting with the R-22 refrigerated air dryers.
6.5.4 Servicing and Decommissioning

Recover refrigerant during servicing using a recovery machine and approved cylinders.
At decommissioning, recover all gas before dismantling and hand it over to an authorised reclaimer / recycler; obtain a recovery or disposal certificate.
Update the F-Gas Register when equipment is added, serviced or removed.
6.5.5 Quantifying Refrigerant Losses in tCO2e
F-gas emissions (tCO2e) = Quantity topped up or lost (kg) × GWP ÷ 1,000
Note: GWP values shall be aligned with the methodology adopted for the Company's GHG inventory.

steps.heading: 6.6 Low-Power Digital Systems and Server Room Practices

body.text: 6.6.1 Server Room and Network Racks

Maintain server room temperature within the ASHRAE recommended range of 18–27 °C instead of overcooling.
Arrange racks in hot aisle / cold aisle layout where possible; use blanking panels and seal cable openings.
Maintain precision ACs and keep server room doors closed.
Meter server room energy separately where practical and track PUE.
6.6.2 Hardware and Infrastructure

Consolidate and virtualise servers; switch off and decommission idle or unused servers.
Use right-sized, high-efficiency UPS systems and enable energy-saving modes where safe.
Prefer ENERGY STAR or BEE star-rated computers, monitors and printers when purchasing.
Consider cloud or hosted services powered by renewable energy when replacing on-premise servers.
6.6.3 End-User Practices

Apply a central power management setting: display off and system sleep after a defined idle time.
Shut down computers, monitors and printers at the end of the working day unless required to run.
Use shared network printers with duplex printing as default.
6.6.4 Disposal of IT Equipment
Obsolete IT equipment shall be disposed of only through authorised e-waste recyclers as per the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, after secure data wiping.

Ensure treated wastewater consistently meets applicable discharge / reuse norms.

steps.heading: 6.3 Toxic Metal Safeguards for Discharge Streams

body.text: 6.3.1 Possible Points of Metal Release

Cleaning of soldering equipment, ribbons or tools carrying solder / flux residues
Washing of floors or equipment in rework, soldering and cell handling areas
Laboratory, testing or maintenance activities using metal-bearing chemicals
Leachate from scrap, battery or hazardous waste storage areas exposed to rain
6.3.2 Prevention at Source

Metal-bearing residues shall be removed by dry cleaning (vacuum, wipes) and managed as hazardous waste, not washed into drains.
Process or chemical wash water shall not be mixed with domestic sewage or sent to the STP.
Scrap, battery and hazardous waste storage areas shall be covered, with impervious flooring and spill containment, so that rainwater does not carry metals into drains.
6.3.3 Metal Capture Techniques

Where a wastewater stream is found to contain heavy metals, it shall be collected separately and treated using a suitable technology before reuse or disposal, or handed over to an authorised treatment facility:

rows: pH adjustment and addition of precipitating / coagulating chemicals convert dissolved metals into solid particles that are settled and removed as sludge
Resin beads exchange harmless ions for dissolved metal ions; resins are regenerated or replaced
Activated carbon or specialised adsorbent media capture metal ions on their surface
Final polishing; removal of trace metals

body.text: Sludge, spent resins and spent adsorbent media from metal treatment shall be managed as hazardous waste through authorised facilities.
6.3.4 Verification

Heavy metal parameters (Pb, Hg, Cd, As, Cr) shall be included in wastewater testing at a defined frequency ([To be confirmed by the Company]).
Any detection above applicable limits shall be treated as a deviation and handled as per Section 7.

sops.title: Hazardous Substance Control and Safe Handling

blocks.text: To define the controls for labelling, storing, handling, transporting, treating and disposing of hazardous substances and hazardous waste, and for training employees, so that exposure of people and releases to the environment are prevented.

It covers all employees, contract workers, transporters and service providers handling these materials.
The Company aims to:

Ensure every hazardous substance is identified, labelled and accompanied by its Safety Data Sheet (SDS).
Store, handle and transport hazardous substances without leaks, spills or exposure.
Treat and dispose of hazardous substances and hazardous waste only through safe and authorised routes.
Ensure all relevant employees are trained and competent.

A current SDS (in a language understood by users) shall be available at the point of storage and use.
No new hazardous substance shall be introduced without HSE review of its SDS.
Suppliers of chemicals shall provide the MSDS with the supply and TREM cards for hazardous chemicals in transit, as required under the EHS clause (clause 22) of the Company's purchase order terms.

Every container, including small dispensing bottles and secondary containers, shall carry a clear, legible label as per GHS showing: product name, hazard pictogram(s), signal word, hazard and precautionary statements, and supplier details.
Labels shall be resistant to the substance and to handling; damaged labels shall be replaced immediately.
Unlabelled containers shall not be used and shall be reported to HSE.
Pipelines and tanks containing hazardous substances shall be identified with content and flow direction.

Store hazardous substances only in designated, ventilated, covered areas with impervious flooring, away from sunlight, heat and ignition sources, as per SDS.
Segregate incompatible substances (e.g. flammables away from oxidisers, acids away from bases).
Use sealed, original or approved containers; keep lids closed when not in use.
Provide secondary containment (spill pallets / bunds) of adequate capacity.
Flammable storage shall have flameproof electrical fittings, earthing and fire extinguishers.
Keep only the minimum quantity required for the shift at the point of use.
Display storage area signage, SDS and emergency contact details.

Move containers in closed condition using trolleys, drum lifters, forklifts or other mechanical aids to avoid manual lifting and dropping.
Use spill-proof carriers and secure containers against tipping during movement.
Transfer and dispense only in designated areas using pumps, funnels or dispensing systems with drip trays.
Protective barriers and restricted access shall be provided around chemical storage and dispensing areas.

Hazardous substances shall be transported only in suitable, labelled, leak-proof packaging by vehicles meeting applicable rules.
Drivers shall carry emergency information (TREM card / SDS) and spill kit as applicable.
Loading and unloading shall be supervised and carried out with the vehicle stationary and secured.

rows: Local exhaust ventilation at soldering, cleaning and dispensing points; enclosed dispensing where practical
Drum lifters, trolleys, pumps and lifts to avoid manual handling of heavy containers
Bunds, guards and restricted-access barriers around storage and dispensing areas
Chemical-resistant gloves, goggles / face shield, apron and respirator as specified in the SDS

Eyewash / safety shower, spill kits and fire extinguishers near storage and use areas

body.text:
Raise the alarm and isolate the area; remove ignition sources.
Wear appropriate PPE and contain the spill with absorbents from the spill kit.
Prevent the spill from entering drains, soil or water.
Collect contaminated absorbent as hazardous waste.
Report the incident to HSE; investigate the cause and record corrective action.

Where safe, residues shall be neutralised or stabilised as per SDS before storage for disposal (e.g. neutralising acid / alkali residues, absorbing liquid residues).
Empty chemical containers shall be drained completely and kept closed; they shall be decontaminated only by a GPCB-licensed decontamination vendor.
Used / spent oil shall be collected in closed containers and reused for suitable alternative applications where possible before disposal.

sops.title: Resource Recovery and Discard Flow Management

blocks.text: To define how the Company gives surplus materials and assets a second life, separates discards at the point of generation, traces each discard flow from origin to final destination and builds workforce awareness of zero-waste practices.

This SOP applies to all waste generated in production, utilities, maintenance, stores, offices, canteen and other areas of the facility, by employees, contract workers and service providers. Detailed controls for hazardous waste disposal are given in the Hazardous Substance Control and Safe Handling SOP, and retired electronics in the Digital Asset Longevity and Retired Electronics Control SOP.
The Company aims to:

Reduce waste generation by reusing, recovering and repurposing materials, equipment and infrastructure.
Segregate all waste at source into defined waste streams.
Maintain a waste stream map showing the route of every stream from generation to final destination.
Increase the share of waste sent for recycling and recovery instead of disposal.
Ensure employees know how to reduce and sort waste correctly.

Systematic tracing of each waste stream from point of generation through collection, storage and transport to final recycling, recovery or disposal

steps.heading: Circular Use of Surplus Materials and Assets

body.text: 6.1 Circular Use of Surplus Materials and Assets
Every material that is no longer needed shall be evaluated in the following order of priority:

Reuse – use again without quality risk.
Rework / Repair – restore to usable condition where technically feasible and cost-effective.
Repurpose – use for a different internal purpose.
Recycle / Recover – send to authorised recyclers.
Dispose – only where none of the above is possible.

rows: Rework where approved by QA; otherwise sent for recycling to authorised recyclers (e.g. Regain, Giga Salvage) under the Company's EPR arrangements

Collected safely and sent to glass recyclers
Pallets redesigned for reuse in module packaging; cartons, wooden pallets and crates reused internally before recycling
Repaired / reconditioned and reused; surplus equipment redeployed to other lines or areas
Usable components recovered from discarded equipment for maintenance spares where safe
Reused for suitable alternative applications before disposal to certified recyclers
Repurposed for storage, offices or other areas

body.text: Quantities reused, recovered and repurposed shall be recorded monthly by Stores and reviewed by HSE.

rows: Paper, office waste, dry domestic waste
Wraps, strapping, EVA / backsheet trims, PVC

Labelled, covered glass bin (handled with PPE)

body.text:
Bins shall be placed at strategic points to cover the entire plant, with pictorial labels.
Mixed or wrongly sorted waste shall be re-sorted by Housekeeping and the issue reported to the area in-charge.
Each stream shall be handed over only to authorised recyclers, collectors or disposal facilities appropriate to that stream.

HSE shall prepare and maintain a waste stream map that traces each stream from where it is generated to its final destination. The map shall be reviewed at least annually and whenever a process, waste type or vendor changes.
The map shall be supported by quantities (kg / tonnes per month) for each stream, so that the efficiency of each step can be assessed and improvement areas identified.

Collection by stream, handling glass and hazardous waste safely

sops.title: Digital Asset Longevity and Retired Electronics Control

blocks.text: To extend the useful life of the Company's IT hardware through refurbishment and remanufacturing, and to ensure that e-waste generated from the Company's own use is sorted, tracked and handed over for proper recycling, so that electronic waste is reduced and fully traceable.

This SOP applies to all IT and electronic equipment used internally by the Company, including desktops, laptops, servers, monitors, printers, network devices, mobile phones, tablets, UPS units, batteries, cables and accessories.

It does not cover electronic waste arising from the products the Company manufactures (solar modules and production scrap), which are managed under the Company's EPR arrangements and the Resource Recovery and Discard Flow Management SOP.
The Company aims to:

Extend the life of IT equipment through repair, upgrade and refurbishment.
Reduce the quantity of electronic waste generated.
Sort internal e-waste by type for effective recycling.
Maintain traceability of every e-waste item from retirement to recycling.

sops.title: Product Care, Longevity and Repair Support

blocks.text: To define how the Company guides customers on getting the best performance and longest life from its solar PV modules, designs modules that deliver more energy with fewer resources, and supports repair so that customers choose repair over replacement wherever possible.

This SOP applies to all solar PV modules manufactured and sold by the Company, including the N-Type TOPCon bifacial dual-glass G12R series (NSG-BFT60 to NSG-BFT132), and to the information, technical support, spare parts and repair services provided to customers, installers, EPC companies and channel partners.
The Company aims to:

Give customers clear guidance on unloading, storage, handling, installation, cleaning and maintenance of modules.
Continuously improve module efficiency and durability so that each module generates more electricity over a longer life.
Make repair practical through diagnostics, spare parts, trained technicians and the warranty process.
Reduce premature replacement of modules in the field.

steps.heading: Owner's Guidance from Storage to Upkeep

body.text: Every customer shall receive, with the product or digitally, the product datasheet, the Installation and User Manual (NS/IM/001), the Module Cleaning Instruction (NSPL/QA/CI/01), the Unloading & Unpacking Instructions (NSPL/ST/SOP/005) and the Limited Warranty Statement. These documents give the following guidance:

rows: Check packaging, model, serial numbers and quantity against the delivery order; prefer forklift over crane; lift only one pallet at a time; drive forklifts at ≤ 5 km/h straight and ≤ 3 km/h when turning; do not unload in winds above Beaufort 6, heavy rain or snow; take photos / videos of unloading for warranty registration

Keep modules in the supplied packaging until installation; secure pallets against movement and falling; do not exceed the marked stacking height (vertical landscape packages not more than two layers); store in a cool, dry place
Handle by the frame, never by the junction box or cables; never step on modules or place loads on them; do not install modules damaged in transit; do not paint, modify or disassemble modules
Keep 10–15 mm clearance between modules; avoid tilt angles below 10–15° so that rain can wash off dirt; avoid shading; follow electrical ratings, grounding and connector instructions of the manual

Clean during low-light hours (early morning / late afternoon) when modules are cool; use soft brush, sponge or micro-fibre cloth and clean (de-ionised / low-mineral) water at ambient temperature; do not use pressure washers, steam, corrosive chemicals, metal objects or abrasives; never clean modules with broken glass or exposed wiring; do not step on modules

Check that cables and connectors are undamaged and secured, no sharp objects touch the module, no unwanted shading, and mounting and grounding parts are tight and free of corrosion; address defects immediately
Register on the "PV Module(s) Owner" portal at www.navitassolar.in within 30 days of purchase

Only periodic cleaning water; no batteries, filters or chemicals

The Company aims to:

Eliminate or minimise restricted substances in products and components.
Ensure every material supplier provides verified material declarations.
Mark products and components so that they can be identified and sorted for recovery.
Increase the share of the module that can be separated and recycled at end of life.

blocks.text: To define how the Company informs users about the correct end-of-life handling of its solar modules and collects used modules back for remanufacturing, recycling or safe disposal, so that materials stay in circulation and are not sent to landfill.

This SOP applies to all solar PV modules sold by the Company that are damaged, obsolete or at the end of their useful life, wherever they are installed, and to the information provided to customers, installers, EPC companies and channel partners.
The Company aims to:

Ensure users know how to return or hand over used modules responsibly.
Collect end-of-life modules free of charge through authorised partners.
Maximise the recovery of glass, aluminium, silicon, copper and other materials.
Prevent uncontrolled disposal and leakage of module components to the environment.

The manual, website and warranty documents shall include end-of-life information covering:

Do not dispose of modules with household or general waste, by burning or by dumping (crossed-out wheelie bin symbol on the module label).
Safe removal: disconnect and isolate the system, cover the module face to stop generation, wear gloves and handle broken glass carefully.
Temporary storage: keep removed modules stacked flat or upright in a dry, covered area; keep broken modules wrapped to prevent glass and material loss.
How to return: contact details and procedure for the Company's free collection service.
What happens next: modules are sent to authorised recyclers where glass, aluminium, silicon, copper and other materials are recovered for new products.

The Company aims to:

Identify and evaluate potential health and safety hazards of products during use.
Provide clear safety information and awareness to everyone who handles the products.
Detect, escalate and contain product safety events without delay.
Communicate promptly and transparently with affected customers and authorities.

Safety labels on modules shall show electrical ratings and warnings against touching live parts and working on energised systems.

Awareness sessions or materials (training for installers and channel partners, safety leaflets, website guidance) shall be provided on safe handling, installation and maintenance.
Product safety information shall be updated when the risk assessment or a safety event identifies new risks.

blocks.text: To define the steps the Company takes to screen, assess, audit and monitor the third parties it works with on environmental, social and governance (ESG) matters, so that ESG risks are identified early and third-party ESG incidents are prevented.

This SOP applies to all third parties the Company engages with, including raw material and component suppliers, service providers, contractors, labour contractors, transporters, distributors, sales representatives, commission agents, brokers, customs brokers and consultants.
The Company aims to:

Communicate ESG expectations to every third party.
Screen third parties for ESG risk before and during the relationship.
Verify ESG performance through self-assessments, internal assessments and on-site audits.
Ensure non-conformities are corrected and improvements are supported.
